questions.stem: What is the name given to the point P in a circle, which is at an equal distance from all points on the circle?
choices: Diameter
Radius
Centre
Circumference
questions.solution: The point P in a circle that is at an equal distance from all points on the circle is called the centre. This is because the centre is the fixed point from which all points on the circle's perimeter are equidistant. The diameter is a line segment through the centre, the radius is the distance from the centre to the perimeter, and the circumference is the distance around the circle.

questions.stem: What is the term used for the distance from the center of a circle to any point on its edge?
choices: Diameter
Radius
Chord
Circumference
questions.solution: The term for the distance from the center of a circle to any point on its edge is defined as the radius. Diameter refers to the distance across the circle through the center, chord is a line segment connecting two points on the circle, and circumference is the total distance around the circle.

questions.stem: In the construction of a rectangle, if one side is 5 cm and the diagonal is 7 cm, what method can be used to find the position of a point that is 7 cm away from one end of the side?
choices: Drawing a straight line of 7 cm from the end and then measuring 5 cm along it
Using a ruler to measure and mark the point
Drawing a circle with radius 7 cm and centre at the end
Drawing a triangle with the side and diagonal as sides
questions.solution: The correct method is to draw a circle with radius 7 cm and centre at the end of the side. This is because all points at a fixed distance from a given point lie on a circle. The other options are incorrect because drawing a straight line or using a ruler leads to inaccuracies, and drawing a triangle is not the most efficient method.
